_doc: OPS-GIT-IDENTITY-CANONICALIZE-W1 — allowlist for scripts/check-author-identity.sh. Every exemption row carries its OWN reason; a reason living only in a comment or in prose gets 'fixed' by a future wave enforcing the contract. Missing, empty or unparseable ⇒ AUTHOR_IDENTITY_VERDICT=INDETERMINATE, exit 3 — never a pass. WE author this file, so empty is a defect in our config, not a fact about the world.
_semantics: ALLOWLIST, not deny-list: an email absent from `allowed` FAILS. `denied` exists so the guard NAMES a known-bad address in its output instead of merely failing to match it — the diagnostic difference between 'not allowed' and 'this is the Gmail we retired on 2026-08-09'.
_scope: core.hooksPath is set --local in crypto-quant-signal-mcp, so this pre-commit block governs that repo and its linked worktrees ONLY. CI identities (ci@algovault.com, github-actions@github.com) and host identities (funnel-snapshot@algovault.com, algovault@hetzner.local, editorial@algovault.com) author commits on machines where this hook is not installed, and are deliberately NOT allowlisted here: allowlisting an identity this guard can never legitimately see would weaken it for zero benefit. If one ever appears locally, that is a real finding.

_out_of_scope_identities_doc: OPS-PROMOTION-INSTRUMENT-INDEPENDENCE-W1 CH2 R2.3. `git log --all` sees every commit on every ref, INCLUDING those authored on machines where this hook is not installed — which _scope already named and deliberately excluded from allowed[]. Counting them as violations would make the git-history instrument produce garbage on its first run. These five are excluded from BOTH the numerator and the denominator, and the excluded count is reported PER IDENTITY, including zeros. An identity in NEITHER allowed[] NOR this list counts as a VIOLATION; that default is deliberate and stays fail-closed. Two such identities exist in history today and were deliberately NOT added here — admin@algovault.com (194 commits, 2026-04-04 -> 2026-07-04) and one personal Gmail (1 commit, 2026-07-03): both were authored ON THIS MACHINE, so under BLOCK they WOULD have been refused, and listing them as out-of-scope would assert something false about where they ran. admin@algovault.com in particular is a VERIFIED email on the AlgoVaultFi account that is deliberately not the commit address (OPS-GIT-IDENTITY-CANONICALIZE-W1-V2 D4) — a legitimate identity with a non-canonical commit address is a violation by definition, not an exemption. Both are out of the current window and therefore inert today; that is a fact to report, never a reason to omit them.

promotion._flip_evidence: PROMOTED report -> block by OPS-AUTHOR-IDENTITY-PROMOTE-W2 at 2026-08-17T02:18:26Z, on a re-measurement taken immediately before this edit rather than trusted from a prior session. PROMOTION_MEASURE_VERDICT=READY, exit 0. Six counts as measured: commits_total_all_refs 1405 · commits_before_measure_from 1317 · commits_in_window 88 · in_window_out_of_scope 1 (funnel-snapshot@algovault.com; the other four declared identities reported 0) · in_window_in_scope 87 (floor min_commits_in_window 30) · in_window_would_be_refused 0 (bar max_violations 0). Secondary population: ledger_indeterminate_in_window 0 (bar max_indeterminate_in_window 0). Date leg: today 2026-08-17 >= not_before 2026-08-16, compared as integer epochs, never as strings. All three legs of `criterion` satisfied independently. Fleet pre-flight at flip time: 40 linked worktrees — 27 carrying script + parseable config, 13 carrying neither and hitting the pre-existing skip-loudly path, and ZERO with script-present-but-config-missing, which is the one failure mode with no per-invocation escape because the shared pre-commit block's guard keys on the SCRIPT only and `warn` does not downgrade an INDETERMINATE. This key records the READING; `reason` above records the DESIGN RATIONALE and is deliberately left byte-identical, so the two are never conflated.
promotion.reason: REPORT-first because a guard that blocks on day one wedges the fleet, and a guard permanently stuck in REPORT is decoration. 7 days rather than the usual 14+ because remediation here is INSTANT AND GLOBAL — CH2 fixed inheritance in one file and CH3 deleted 11 local overrides in one pass — unlike gate-staleness, whose per-worktree healing depends on each checkout rebasing and measurably did not converge over 24h.
promotion.criterion: THREE conditions, never collapsed: in_window_would_be_refused must be <= max_violations, in-window INDETERMINATE rows must be <= max_indeterminate_in_window, AND today must be >= not_before. A numeric bar alone can be met on day one by a machine nobody committed from; a date bar alone promotes a guard that is still firing. The violation count is MEASURED FROM GIT HISTORY — commits on all refs, bucketed by author email — not from the ledger this gate writes. See instrument{} for why.
promotion._measure_from_reason: SET to 2026-08-09T11:07:26Z, the committer timestamp of 24419af, the LAST commit of the OPS-GIT-IDENTITY-CANONICALIZE-W1-V2 remediation (CH5 baseline). The comparison is >=, so 24419af itself is in scope. Before that instant identities on this machine were unremediated; after it they were not — the boundary is an EVENT a reader can verify by resolving one SHA. It replaces 2026-08-09T11:30:00Z, which was a round-number cushion 23 minutes later: arbitrary, unverifiable, and precisely the shape _window_boundary_law exists to forbid. The tighter boundary also GROWS the denominator (80 -> 83 in-scope commits at CH2 time), which is free evidence. HISTORICAL NOTE, kept because it is why the window exists at all: OPS-AUTHOR-IDENTITY-PROMOTE-W1 found 4 FAIL + 3 INDETERMINATE ledger rows all bearing one timestamp (2026-08-09T10:55:51Z) and one repo root — the worktree that BUILT the guard. They are that wave's AC4.2/4.3/4.4 evidence, the acceptance tests that PROVED the guard can fail. Proving a guard can fail necessarily writes FAIL rows, so THE INSTRUMENT CONTAINED ITS OWN CALIBRATION, and a bar measured over the whole ledger conflated calibration with operation in perpetuity. CH2 retires that defect at the root rather than working around it: git history contains no calibration rows because a deliberate gate run creates no commit. Explicitly REJECTED alternative, then and now: raising max_violations to 4. That bakes the calibration count into the threshold, so 4 REAL violations would also pass — a window SEPARATES the two populations, a raised bar MERGES them.
promotion._window_boundary_law: A promotion window boundary may be SET or MOVED only across a change in what a row means (the instrument's semantics) or a change in the population being measured (a remediation), and never across an inconvenient individual observation. The test: can the boundary be defined without reference to the row you want excluded? OPS-AUTHOR-IDENTITY-PROMOTE-W1 refused to advance past 2026-08-16T04:42:06Z and was right — the only available justification was that one row was in the way, and the advance left ~0 rows, which the sample floor correctly returned as INDETERMINATE. This boundary is definable without reference to any commit: before it, identities were unremediated; after it, they were not.
promotion._min_commits_in_window_reason: A window with no sample floor is a free pass: set measure_from to yesterday and the criterion is trivially satisfiable by an empty window — the vacuity hole in the shape of a date. Fewer than min_commits_in_window IN-SCOPE commits after the cut is INDETERMINATE, never READY: too few observations is 'we have not looked', which is not 'we looked and it was clean'. 30 matches the house convention (report_class_promotion.runs_required, mode2_promotion.runs_required) and 83 in-scope commits were available when CH2 re-pointed the instrument, so it is satisfiable today rather than aspirational. RENAMED from min_rows_in_window by OPS-PROMOTION-INSTRUMENT-INDEPENDENCE-W1 CH2 R2.2 — the sample-floor argument is unchanged and is what stopped the last wave from cheating; only the unit moved, from ledger ROWS to git COMMITS. The old key must be ABSENT, not merely superseded: a rename that leaves the old key behind is a duplicate source of truth.
promotion._max_indeterminate_reason: Flipping to BLOCK converts INDETERMINATE from logged into COMMIT REFUSED, and the rollback record already establishes that ALGOVAULT_AUTHOR_IDENTITY=warn does NOT free an INDETERMINATE — emit() downgrades only a FAIL. So a live INDETERMINATE rate would wedge sessions with no per-invocation escape. Git history cannot see verdicts, only commits, so THIS ONE BAR IS MEASURED FROM THE LEDGER — a legitimate grade-B role for a secondary population, declared as secondary in instrument.reason rather than quietly reused. Measured at CH2: 0 INDETERMINATE rows in the window against 74 PASS and 1 FAIL, so the bar of 0 is satisfiable today.
promotion._shape_note: This block deliberately does NOT match the {runs_required, escalate_after} shape that scripts/lib/promotion-bound.mjs asserts on freshness_promotion, report_class_promotion and mode2_promotion. The divergence is INTENTIONAL: that shape measures RUNS against an ESCALATION DATE; this one, {max_violations, max_indeterminate_in_window, not_before, measure_from, min_commits_in_window}, measures VIOLATIONS against a START BOUND. Do not 'unify' them — assertPromotionBound would throw on this block, and the unification would be the same mistake as collapsing claudemd-claim-config's two criteria with two owners into one. CORRECTED by OPS-PROMOTION-INSTRUMENT-INDEPENDENCE-W1: this note used to say 'Two criterion shapes exist in this repo'. Measured by scanning ops/*.json, there are FOUR shapes across SEVEN promotion blocks. What is shape-INDEPENDENT is instrument{} — assertInstrumentIndependence reads only that, which is why it can cover this block while the shape assertion must never be pointed at it.
promotion._reader: scripts/check-author-identity.sh --measure-promotion. Every field here has a live consumer: measure_from, min_commits_in_window and max_violations drive the git-history computation; max_indeterminate_in_window drives the ledger-side bar; out_of_scope_identities[] drives the per-identity exclusion. The flag prints six counts plus PROMOTION_MEASURE_VERDICT=READY|BLOCKED|INDETERMINATE (exit 0/1/3) and returns via a `case` BEFORE the gate body, so it never evaluates an identity and never appends a ledger row. Dead config is config with no reader, and this repo's law says every field has >=1 live consumer. NOTE: this block has NO JavaScript consumer, so assertInstrumentIndependence is NOT called on it by any gate — its enforcement is tests/unit/promotion-independence.test.ts, which discovers it by scanning ops/*.json and runs on the existing pre-push vitest gate. That is deliberate and is why this wave needed no hook change.

instrument.population: Commits on ALL refs, bucketed by AUTHOR email against allowed[] and out_of_scope_identities[] — `git log --all`, compared on INTEGER EPOCH SECONDS (%ct) against measure_from.
instrument.written_by: git — every commit is written by the act of committing, and NOTHING this gate does creates one.
instrument.reason: GRADE A: the population is independent of the subject. A deliberate invocation of this gate — including `--measure-promotion` itself, and including a run with GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=test@test.local — creates no commit, so it CANNOT ENTER THE POPULATION AT ALL. That is the defect this wave existed to retire: on 2026-08-16T04:42:06Z a manual run wrote a FAIL row into the ledger that measured this very gate, and OPS-AUTHOR-IDENTITY-PROMOTE-W1 HALTed on it. Under the ledger the pollution had to be FILTERED; under git history it is structurally absent. Three further properties come free: completeness (every commit, by definition, rather than every invocation-if-no-append-fails), durability (committed and reviewable, rather than a local file that dies with the checkout), and RETROACTIVITY — the verdict is computable over any past window immediately, instead of after N new rows accumulate, which is what turns OPS-AUTHOR-IDENTITY-PROMOTE-W2 from a multi-day wait into a decision available now. SECONDARY POPULATION, named rather than quietly reused: git history cannot see verdicts, only commits, so max_indeterminate_in_window alone is measured from $GIT_COMMON_DIR/algovault-author-identity.log. That is a grade-B role — the ledger is a cache of verdicts whose INDETERMINATE rate is re-observable by re-running the gate — and it bounds a failure mode (a wedged commit path under BLOCK) that the primary population is structurally blind to. It is never used for the violation count.
